title: Irrelevant context change
intent: Stability control. The Clifton kit note changes: accurate, dated, and with no bearing on the decision. The advice must come back byte-identical to the complete-evidence run — not rewritten, not reworded, not re-prioritised.
fixture_expected_checks: The actionable content of the wide-channel advice is unchanged from the complete-evidence run.
Any variation is reported as observed run-to-run variance, not as a response to the kit change.

not_applicable_reasons.U2: Tactical support is present in this variant; the opponent observation is intact.
not_applicable_reasons.R1: Generation only; there is no prior run whose recommendation IDs could be referenced.
not_applicable_reasons.R2: Generation only; no availability override is applied, and requiring a revision here would reward churn.
not_applicable_reasons.R4: Generation only; there is no rerun against which to compare the snapshot.

human_review.question: Where the advice does differ from the baseline run, is the difference plausibly ordinary run-to-run variance, or has the model treated the kit note as decision-relevant?

notes: EWE-62 models this as a data change rather than an availability override, and the property it asserts is a comparison against the complete-evidence run. R3 therefore compares the multiset of actionable content across the two runs rather than matching recommendation IDs, which do not carry across independent runs. A difference is reported as a finding, not silently attributed to the kit change.
